# Ordinal Numbers (서수) - Korean Perspective

한국인이 한국어 서수 어휘를 학습할 때 + 일본어 번역 비교. 10 entries (첫째~열째) 와 한자어 비교.

## 서수 (Ordinal Numbers)

| 한국어 | 일어 | 일어 IPA |
|---|---|---|
| 첫째 (cheotjjae) | 一番目 (いちばんめ, ichibanme) | /i.tɕi.baɴ.me/ |
| 둘째 (duljjae) | 二番目 (にばんめ, nibanme) | /ni.baɴ.me/ |
| 셋째 (setjjae) | 三番目 (さんばんめ, sanbanme) | /sam.baɴ.me/ |
| 넷째 (netjjae) | 四番目 (よんばんめ, yonbanme) | /jon.baɴ.me/ |
| 다섯째 (daseotjjae) | 五番目 (ごばんめ, gobanme) | /ɡo.baɴ.me/ |
| 여섯째 (yeoseotjjae) | 六番目 (ろくばんめ, rokubanme) | /ɾo.kɯ.baɴ.me/ |
| 일곱째 (ilgopjjae) | 七番目 (ななばんめ, nanabanme) | /na.na.baɴ.me/ |
| 여덟째 (yeodeoljjae) | 八番目 (はちばんめ, hachibanme) | /ha.tɕi.baɴ.me/ |
| 아홉째 (ahopjjae) | 九番目 (くばんめ, kubanme) | /kɯ.baɴ.me/ |
| 열째 (yeoljjae) | 十番目 (じゅうばんめ, jūbanme) | /dʑɯː.baɴ.me/ |

## 한국어 학습 노트

**한국어 서수 = 순 우리말 + 접미사 '째' (째)**: 첫째 (첫 + 짜) / 둘째 (둘 + 짜) 등. **일어 서수 = 한자어 + 접미사 '目 (め)'**: 一番目 (いち + ばん + め) / 二番目 (に + ばん + め) 등. **韓 서수 접미사 '째' (chae)** = **日 서수 접미사 '目 (め, me)** 어원 비교.

# career vocabulary - English theme

**Source:** [[work-and-career]]
**Theme:** Work & Career — job titles, office vocabulary, meetings, emails, professional language
**Level:** A2-B2

English vocabulary for the workplace — job titles, meetings, deadlines, projects, email phrases, and business etiquette. Useful for professionals in international environments.

---

### work

**Part of Speech:** noun / verb

**Definition:** 일 / 일하다

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /wɜːrk/

**Etymology:** From Old English *weorc* "something done, act, deed."

#### Examples

- I go to work at 9 AM.
- She works hard.

#### Related Terms

- Related: [[career-vocabulary]]

#### Sources

- [[work-and-career]]

---

### office

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** 사무실

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈɒfɪs/

**Etymology:** From Latin *officium* "service, duty."

#### Examples

- I work in an office downtown.
- The office is on the 5th floor.

#### Sources

- [[work-and-career]]

---

### meeting

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** 회의

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈmiːtɪŋ/

**Etymology:** *meet* + *-ing*.

#### Examples

- We have a meeting at 2 PM.
- The meeting ran over time.

#### Sources

- [[work-and-career]]

---

### manager

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** 매니저 / 관리자

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈmænɪdʒər/

**Etymology:** From Italian *maneggiare* "to handle."

#### Examples

- I'll ask my manager.
- She is the new project manager.

#### Sources

- [[work-and-career]]

---

### project

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** 프로젝트

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈprɒdʒɛkt/

**Etymology:** From Latin *projectum* "something thrown forth."

#### Examples

- We're working on a new project.
- The project deadline is next month.

#### Sources

- [[work-and-career]]

---

### deadline

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** 마감 / 데드라인

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈdɛdlaɪn/

**Etymology:** *dead* + *line*.

#### Examples

- The deadline is Friday.
- We can't meet the deadline.

#### Sources

- [[work-and-career]]

---

### report

**Part of Speech:** noun / verb

**Definition:** 보고서 / 보고하다

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /rɪˈpɔːrt/

**Etymology:** From Latin *reportare* "to carry back."

#### Examples

- I need to write a report.
- She reported to her supervisor.

#### Sources

- [[work-and-career]]

---

### email

**Part of Speech:** noun / verb

**Definition:** 이메일

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈiːmeɪl/

**Etymology:** *electronic* + *mail*.

#### Examples

- I'll send you an email.
- Please email me the details.

#### Sources

- [[work-and-career]]

---

### salary

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** 급여 (월급)

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈsæləri/

**Etymology:** From Latin *salarium* "salt money."

#### Examples

- What's the salary for this position?
- They offer a competitive salary.

#### Sources

- [[work-and-career]]

---

### colleague

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** 동료

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈkɒliːɡ/

**Etymology:** From Latin *collega* "partner in office."

#### Examples

- My colleagues are very helpful.
- I'll introduce you to my colleagues.

#### Sources

- [[work-and-career]]

---

### boss

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** 상사 / boss

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /bɒs/

**Etymology:** From Dutch *baas* "master."

#### Examples

- My boss is on vacation.
- I'll ask my boss for time off.

#### Sources

- [[work-and-career]]

---

### employee

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** 직원

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ɪmˈplɔɪiː/

**Etymology:** From French *employé* "employed."

#### Examples

- We have 50 employees.
- She's a former employee.

#### Sources

- [[work-and-career]]

---

### interview

**Part of Speech:** noun / verb

**Definition:** 인터뷰 / 면접

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈɪntərvjuː/

**Etymology:** From French *entrevue*.

#### Examples

- I have a job interview tomorrow.
- She interviewed five candidates.

#### Sources

- [[work-and-career]]

---

### resume

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** 이력서 (resume)

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /rɪˈzuːm/

**Etymology:** From French *résumé* "summary."

#### Examples

- Please send your resume.
- I updated my resume.

#### Cultural Notes

US uses "resume"; UK uses "CV" (curriculum vitae).

#### Sources

- [[work-and-career]]

---

### schedule

**Part of Speech:** noun / verb

**Definition:** 일정 / 예약하다

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈʃɛdjuːl/

**Etymology:** From Latin *schedula* "small piece of paper."

#### Examples

- Let's schedule a meeting.
- Check your schedule.

#### Sources

- [[work-and-career]]

---

### agenda

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** 의제 / 안건

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /əˈdʒɛndə/

**Etymology:** From Latin *agenda* "things to be done."

#### Examples

- What's on the agenda?
- Let's set the agenda.

#### Sources

- [[work-and-career]]

---

### presentation

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** 프레젠테이션 / 발표

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˌprɛzənˈteɪʃn/

**Etymology:** From Latin *praesentare* "to place before."

#### Examples

- I have a presentation tomorrow.
- She gave a great presentation.

#### Sources

- [[work-and-career]]

---

### feedback

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** 피드백

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈfiːdbæk/

**Etymology:** *feed* + *back*.

#### Examples

- Could you give me some feedback?
- I appreciate your feedback.

#### Sources

- [[work-and-career]]

---

### overtime

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** 초과 근무

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈoʊvərtaɪm/

**Etymology:** *over* + *time*.

#### Examples

- I worked overtime last week.
- Overtime pay is 1.5x regular salary.

#### Sources

- [[work-and-career]]

---

# Business (비즈니스) - Korean Perspective

한국인이 한국어 비즈니스 어휘를 학습할 때 + 일본어 번역 비교. 39+ 어휘 (이메일/회의/직장) 와 일본어 비즈니스 정중어 비교.

**참고:** 본 페이지는 `wiki/Korean/vocabulary/business-vocabulary.md` 의 한국어 관점 + 일본어 번역 페이지.

---

## 이메일 (Email)

### 이메일 (imeil)

**일어:** メール (mēru) / Eメール (ī-mēru) — 한국어 "이메일" / 일어 "メール" 의미.

**IPA:** /i.me.il/ / 일어 /meː.ɾɯ/ / /iː.meː.ɾɯ/

#### 한국어 학습 노트

**이메일 (imeil)** = 일어 "メール (mēru)" 의미. **英語 email → 한국어 직접 차용 + 日 カタカナ 転写** 어원 비교.

---

### 주소 (juso)

**일어:** 住所 (じゅうしょ, juusho) — 한국어 "주소" / 일어 "住所" 의미.

**IPA:** /dʑu.so/ / 일어 /dʑɯː.ɕo/

#### 한국어 학습 노트

**주소 (juso)** = 일어 "住所 (juusho)" 의미. **한자어 어원 비교**.

---

### 보내는 사람 (보내는 사람)

**일어:** 送信者 (そうしんしゃ) — 한국어 "보내는 사람" / 일어 "送信者" 의미.

**IPA:** /bo.na.nɯn sa.ɾam/ / 일어 /soː.ɕiɴ.ɕa/

#### 한국어 학습 노트

**보내는 사람 (send-person)** = 일어 "送信者 (soushinsha)" 의미. **한자어 어원 비교**.

---

### 받는 사람 (받는 사람)

**일어:** 受信者 (じゅしんしゃ) — 한국어 "받는 사람" / 일어 "受信者" 의미.

**IPA:** /ban.nɯn sa.ɾam/ / 일어 /dʑɯ.ɕiɴ.ɕa/

#### 한국어 학습 노트

**받는 사람 (receive-person)** = 일어 "受信者 (jushinsha)" 의미.

---

### 제목 (제목)

**일어:** 件名 (けんめい, kenmei) — 한국어 "제목" / 일어 "件名" 의미.

**IPA:** /dʑe.mok̚/ / 일어 /ken.meː/

#### 한국어 학습 노트

**제목 (jemok)** = 일어 "件名 (kenmei)" 의미. **件 (건, 건)** 의 어원: 件 + 名 (명, 이름) = 제목.

---

### 첨부 (첨부)

**일어:** 添付 (てんぷ, tenpu) — 한국어 "첨부" / 일어 "添付" 의미.

**IPA:** /tɕʰʌm.bu/ / 일어 /ten.pɯ/

#### 한국어 학습 노트

**첨부 (cheombu)** = 일어 "添付 (tenpu)" 의미. **한자어 어원 비교**.

---

### 보내다 (보내다)

**일어:** 送る (おくる, okuru) — 한국어 "보내다" / 일어 "送る" 의미.

**IPA:** /bo.na.da/ / 일어 /o.kɯ.ɾɯ/

#### 한국어 학습 노트

**보내다 (bonaeda)** = 일어 "送る (okuru)" 의미. **音읽 送 (そう, 송)** = 한국어 "송" 어원 비교.

---

### 받다 (받다)

**일어:** 受け取る (うけとる, uketoru) — 한국어 "받다" / 일어 "受け取る" 의미.

**IPA:** /bat̚.da/ / 일어 /ɯ.ke.to.ɾɯ/

#### 한국어 학습 노트

**받다 (batda)** = 일어 "受け取る (uketoru)" 의미. **한자어 受 (수)** = 한국어 "수" 어원 비교.

---

### 답장 (답장)

**일어:** 返信 (へんしん, henshin) — 한국어 "답장" / 일어 "返信" 의미.

**IPA:** /tap̚.tɕaŋ/ / 일어 /hen.ɕiɴ/

#### 한국어 학습 노트

**답장 (dapjang)** = 일어 "返信 (henshin)" 의미. **한자어 返 (반) + 信 (신)** 의 어원 비교.

---

### 저장 (저장)

**일어:** 保存 (ほぞん, hozon) — 한국어 "저장" / 일어 "保存" 의미.

**IPA:** /tɕʌ.dʑaŋ/ / 일어 /ho.zoɴ/

#### 한국어 학습 노트

**저장 (jeojang)** = 일어 "保存 (hozon)" 의미. **한자어 어원 비교**.

---

### 삭제 (삭제)

**일어:** 削除 (さくじょ, sakujyo) — 한국어 "삭제" / 일어 "削除" 의미.

**IPA:** /sak̚.tɕe/ / 일어 /sa.kɯ.dʑo/

#### 한국어 학습 노트

**삭제 (sakje)** = 일어 "削除 (sakujyo)" 의미. **한자어 어원 비교**.

---

## 회의 (Meetings)

### 회의 (회의)

**일어:** 会議 (かいぎ, kaigi) — 한국어 "회의" / 일어 "会議" 의미.

**IPA:** /hwe.ɕʰi/ / 일어 /ka.i.ɡi/

#### 한국어 학습 노트

**회의 (hoeeui)** = 일어 "会議 (kaigi)" 의미. **한자어 會 (회) + 議 (의)** 어원 비교.

---

### 일정 (일정)

**일어:** スケジュール (sukejūru) — 한국어 "일정" / 일어 "スケジュール" 의미.

**IPA:** /il.tɕʌŋ/ / 일어 /sɯ.ke.dʑɯː.ɾɯ/

#### 한국어 학습 노트

**일정 (iljeong)** = 일어 "スケジュール (sukejūru)" 의미. **英語 schedule → 한자어 일정 + 日 カタカナ 転写** 어원 비교.

---

### 의제 (의제)

# body-vocabulary — Body Parts

**Source:** Oxford 3000 (CEFR A1-A2) + OEC frequency list
**Theme:** body-vocabulary
**Level:** A1-A2

Essential body part vocabulary for beginner English learners. Sourced from Oxford 3000 word list (CEFR A1-A2) and the Oxford English Corpus (OEC) frequency rankings. Each entry is foundational vocabulary for describing health, appearance, and physical sensation.

---

## Head & Face

### head

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the upper part of the body, containing the brain, eyes, ears, nose, and mouth

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /hɛd/

**Etymology:** Old English "heafod", from Proto-Germanic *haubudą. Cognate with German "Haupt".

#### Examples

- My head hurts. — 머리가 아파요.
- She nodded her head. — 그녀가 고개를 끄덕였다.

#### Related Terms

- ''brain''
- ''skull''
- ''forehead''

#### Cultural Notes

In English, "head" is metonymically used for "mind" or "intelligence" (e.g., "use your head", "a head for heights"). In Korean translations, this is often rendered as "머리" but the English idiom may map better to "머리를 써" (use your brain).

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### face

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the front part of a person's head, from forehead to chin

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /feɪs/

**Etymology:** From Old French "face", from Latin "facies" (form, appearance, face).

#### Examples

- She has a round face. — 그녀는 둥근 얼굴을 가졌다.
- Wash your face. — 얼굴을 씻어.

#### Related Terms

- ''forehead''
- ''cheek''
- ''chin''
- ''jaw''

#### Cultural Notes

In English idioms, "face" carries strong social meaning: "lose face" (체면 잃다), "save face" (체면을 살리다), "face-to-face" (직접, 대면으로). These are loan translations of East Asian concepts into English.

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### eye

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** each of a pair of globular organs of sight in the head

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /aɪ/

**Etymology:** Old English "ēage", from Proto-Germanic *augō. Cognate with German "Auge".

#### Examples

- She has blue eyes. — 그녀는 파란 눈을 가졌다.
- Keep your eyes open. — 눈을 뜨고 있어.

#### Related Terms

- ''eyebrow''
- ''eyelash''
- ''pupil''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### ear

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the organ of hearing and balance in humans and other vertebrates

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ɪər/

**Etymology:** Old English "ēare", from Proto-Germanic *auzō. Cognate with German "Ohr".

#### Examples

- I have an ear infection. — 귀가 감염됐다.
- She has good ears for music. — 그녀는 음악에 귀가 밝다.

#### Related Terms

- ''eardrum''
- ''hearing''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### nose

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the part of the face above the mouth, containing the nostrils and used for breathing and smelling

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /noʊz/

**Etymology:** Old English "nosu", from Proto-Germanic *nusō. Cognate with German "Nase".

#### Examples

- He has a big nose. — 그는 코가 크다.
- She blew her nose. — 그녀는 코를 풀었다.

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### mouth

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the opening in the human or animal face through which food is taken and from which sounds are emitted

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /maʊθ/

**Etymology:** Old English "mūth", from Proto-Germanic *munthaz. Cognate with German "Mund".

#### Examples

- Open your mouth. — 입을 열어.
- She covered her mouth. — 그녀는 입을 막았다.

#### Related Terms

- ''lip''
- ''tongue''
- ''tooth''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

## Torso

### chest

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the front surface of the upper body, from the neck to the abdomen

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /tʃɛst/

**Etymology:** Old English "cest" (box, coffin), from Proto-Germanic *kistō. Original meaning was "container"; modern anatomical sense from 16th c. Distinguish from "breast" (가슴, mammary).

#### Examples

- He has a broad chest. — 그는 가슴이 넓다.
- She has a pain in her chest. — 그녀는 가슴이 아프다.

#### Related Terms

- ''breast''
- ''rib''
- ''heart''

#### Cultural Notes

Korean "가슴" can mean both "chest" and "breast" — English distinguishes. For health/anatomy, prefer "chest". For mammary context, "breast". For emotional context (e.g., "가슴이 아프다"), "heart" or "chest" both work.

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### back

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the rear surface of the human body from the shoulders to the hips

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /bæk/

**Etymology:** Old English "bæc", from Proto-Germanic *baką. Cognate with German "Bach" (back, brook — different semantic shift).

#### Examples

- My back hurts. — 등이 아파요.
- She carried the baby on her back. — 그녀는 아기를 등에 업었다.

#### Related Terms

- ''spine''
- ''shoulder''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### stomach

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the internal organ in which the first part of digestion occurs

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈstʌmək/

**Etymology:** From Latin "stomachus", from Greek "stomakhos" (gullet), from "stoma" (mouth). Spelling influenced by Latin.

#### Examples

- I have a stomach ache. — 배가 아파요.
- My stomach is full. — 배가 부르다.

#### Related Terms

- ''belly'' (informal)
- ''abdomen''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

## Limbs

### arm

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** each of the two upper limbs of the human body from the shoulder to the hand

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ɑːrm/

**Etymology:** Old English "arm", from Proto-Germanic *armaz. Cognate with German "Arm".

#### Examples

- She broke her arm. — 그녀는 팔을 부러뜨렸다.
- He carried the box under his arm. — 그는 팔 밑에 상자를 들고 갔다.

#### Related Terms

- ''elbow''
- ''wrist''
- ''shoulder''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### hand

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the end of the human arm beyond the wrist, including the palm, fingers, and thumb

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /hænd/

**Etymology:** Old English "hand", from Proto-Germanic *handuz. Cognate with German "Hand".

#### Examples

- Wash your hands. — 손을 씻어.
- Give me a hand. — 도와줘.

#### Related Terms

- ''finger''
- ''palm''
- ''thumb''
- ''nail''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### leg

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** each of the limbs on which a person or animal walks

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /lɛɡ/

**Etymology:** From Old Norse "leggr" (leg, limb). Replaced Old English "shank".

#### Examples

- She hurt her leg. — 그녀는 다리를 다쳤다.
- He crossed his legs. — 그는 다리를 꼬았다.

#### Related Terms

- ''knee''
- ''ankle''
- ''foot''
- ''thigh''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### foot

**Part of Speech:** noun (plural: feet)

**Definition:** the lower extremity of the leg below the ankle, on which a person stands or walks

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /fʊt/ (plural: /fiːt/)

**Etymology:** Old English "fōt", from Proto-Germanic *fōts. Cognate with German "Fuß".

#### Examples

- I hurt my foot. — 발을 다쳤어요.
- She stood on one foot. — 그녀는 한 발로 섰다.

#### Related Terms

- ''toe''
- ''heel''
- ''ankle''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

## Other Essentials

### finger

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** each of the four slender jointed parts attached to either hand

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /ˈfɪŋɡər/

**Etymology:** Old English "finger", from Proto-Germanic *fingraz. Cognate with German "Finger".

#### Examples

- She pointed her finger. — 그녀는 손가락으로 가리켰다.
- I cut my finger. — 손가락을 베었어요.

#### Related Terms

- ''thumb''
- ''index finger''
- ''nail''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

### neck

**Part of Speech:** noun

**Definition:** the part of a person's body connecting the head to the rest of the body

**Pronunciation / IPA:** /nɛk/

**Etymology:** Old English "hnecca" (back of neck), from Proto-Germanic *hnekk-. Cognate with German "Nacken".

#### Examples

- My neck is stiff. — 목이 뻣뻣해요.
- She wore a necklace around her neck. — 그녀는 목에 목걸이를 했다.

#### Related Terms

- ''throat''
- ''shoulder''

#### Sources

- [[body-vocabulary]]

---

# Months (월) - Korean Perspective

한국인이 한국어 월 어휘를 학습할 때 + 일본어 번역 비교. 10 entries (1月~10月) 와 한자어 비교.

## 월 (Months)

| 한국어 | 일어 | 일어 IPA |
|---|---|---|
| 1월 (1wol) | 一月 (いちがつ, ichigatsu) | /i.tɕi.gat.tsɯ/ |
| 2월 (2wol) | 二月 (にがつ, nigatsu) | /ni.gat.tsɯ/ |
| 3월 (3wol) | 三月 (さんがつ, sangatsu) | /san.gat.tsɯ/ |
| 4월 (4wol) | 四月 (しがつ, shigatsu) | /ɕi.gat.tsɯ/ |
| 5월 (5wol) | 五月 (ごがつ, gogatsu) | /ɡo.gat.tsɯ/ |
| 6월 (6wol) | 六月 (ろくがつ, rokugatsu) | /ɾo.kɯ.gat.tsɯ/ |
| 7월 (7wol) | 七月 (しちがつ, shichigatsu) | /ɕi.tɕi.gat.tsɯ/ |
| 8월 (8wol) | 八月 (はちがつ, hachigatsu) | /ha.tɕi.gat.tsɯ/ |
| 9월 (9wol) | 九月 (くがつ, kugatsu) | /kɯ.gat.tsɯ/ |
| 10월 (10wol) | 十月 (じゅうがつ, jūgatsu) | /dʑɯː.gat.tsɯ/ |

## 한국어 학습 노트

**한국어 월 (月) = 일어 月 (がつ)** 어원 비교. **한국어 4월 = 일어 四月 (しがつ)** 발음 변이 (韓 사 vs 日 시). **韓 7월 = 日 七月 (しちがつ)** 발음 변이 (韓 칠 vs 日 시치). **韓 9월 = 日 九月 (くがつ)** 발음 변이 (韓 구 vs 日 쿠). **음읽 발음 변이 (4/7/9)** 비교.

# greetings (Korean) expressions

**Overview:** Korean greetings 표현. 일상적 인사 패턴 모음.

### 안녕하세요!

**Category:** greeting

**Usage:** 안녕하세요!

**Example:** 안녕하세요! 잘 지내세요?

---

### 좋은 아침이에요!

**Category:** greeting

**Usage:** 좋은 아침입니다!

**Example:** 좋은 아침이에요! 잘 잤어요?

---

### 좋은 오후예요!

**Category:** greeting

**Usage:** 좋은 오후입니다!

**Example:** 좋은 오후예요! 하루 어때요?

---

### 좋은 저녁이에요!

**Category:** greeting

**Usage:** 좋은 저녁입니다!

**Example:** 좋은 저녁이에요! 일 어땠어요?

**Category:** greeting

**Usage:** 안녕히 주무세요!

business-basics.md.body:
# Expressions: Business Basics (한국어)

> **Theme:** Business & Professional
> **Level:** B1-C1 (formal)
> **Standard:** 표준어 (Pyojuneo, Standard Korean)

Korean business communication — greetings, email/meeting phrases, negotiations, contracts.

---

## 안녕하세요

(See daily-life)

---

## 감사합니다

(See daily-life)

---

## 죄송합니다

(See daily-life)

---

## 잘 부탁드립니다

**Part of Speech:** expression (formal request, greeting)
**Definition:** "Please take care of me" — 가장 격식 있는 인사와 부탁.
**Form:** Jal butak deurimnida.

### Usage

비즈니스 첫 만남, 이메일/문자 시작/끝, 격식 부탁.

### Variations

- **잘 부탁드립니다 (Jal butak deurimnida)** — "Please take care of me" (default 격식)
- **잘 부탁해요 (Jal butakhaeyo)** — "Please take care of me" (정중)
- **잘 부탁해 (Jal butakhae)** — 캐주얼 (친구/동료)
- **부탁드립니다 (Butak deurimnida)** — "Please" (간결)
- **많은 도움 부탁드립니다 (Manyu doum butak deurimnida)** — "Please help me a lot"

### Sample Sentences

- **저희 회사와 잘 부탁드립니다 (Jeohui hoewa jal butak deurimnida)** — "Please take care of our company"
- **앞으로도 잘 부탁드립니다 (Apeurodo jal butak deurimnida)** — "Please continue to take care of me"

### Cultural Notes

- **비즈니스**: 가장 흔한 격식 인사
- **이메일 끝**: "감사합니다, 잘 부탁드립니다" — 두 표현 함께 사용
- **첫 만남**: 명함 교환 시 "잘 부탁드립니다"
- **일본어 "よろしくお願いします (yoroshiku onegaishimasu)"**와 일치

### Sources

- `[[Language/wiki/comparative/business-email]]`
- `[[Language/wiki/comparative/politeness-honorifics]]`

---

## 수고하셨습니다

**Part of Speech:** expression (greeting, workplace)
**Definition:** "Thank you for your hard work" — 직장/동료 표준 인사.
**Form:** Sugo hasyeotseumnida.

### Usage

직장, 회의 종료, 프로젝트 완료.

### Variations

- **수고하셨습니다 (Sugo hasyeotseumnida)** — "Thank you for hard work" (default)
- **수고했어요 (Sugohaesseoyo)** — 캐주얼
- **수고하셨어요 (Sugohasyeosseoyo)** — 캐주얼 변형
- **수고해요 (Sugohaeyo)** — 매우 캐주얼
- **고생하셨습니다 (Gosaeng hasyeotseumnida)** — 격식 (동사)

### Sample Sentences

- **수고하셨습니다, 오늘 회의 마무리 (Sugo hasyeotseumnida, oneul hoeui mamuri)** — "Thank you for your work, ending today's meeting"
- **모두 수고하셨습니다 (Modu sugo hasyeotseumnida)** — "Everyone, thanks for hard work"

### Cultural Notes

- **매일 아침/저녁**: 출근/퇴근 인사
- **상사**: "수고하셨습니다" 정중
- **동료**: "수고했어" / "수고" 캐주얼
- **일본어 "お疲れ様でした"**와 일치

### Sources

- `[[Language/wiki/comparative/cultural-values]]`

---

## 검토하겠습니다

**Part of Speech:** expression (decision)
**Definition:** "I'll review/consider it" — 부드러운 보류.
**Form:** Geomto hagetseumnida.

### Usage

상사/고객의 요청에 즉답 못할 때.

### Variations

- **검토하겠습니다 (Geomto hagetseumnida)** — "I'll review" (default)
- **검토 후 답변 드리겠습니다 (Geomto hu dapdun deurigetseumnida)** — "I'll answer after review"
- **내일까지 검토해 보겠습니다 (Naeilkkaji geomtohae bogetseumnida)** — "I'll review by tomorrow"
- **신중히 검토하겠습니다 (Sinjunghi geomto hagetseumnida)** — "I'll carefully review" (강조)

### Sample Sentences

- **요청 사항 검토하겠습니다 (Yocheong saenghwan geomto hagetseumnida)** — "I'll review your request"
- **내일까지 검토 후 연락 드리겠습니다 (Naeilkkaji geomto hu yeollak deurigetseumnida)** — "I'll contact you by tomorrow after review"

### Cultural Notes

- **"검토" = "consider"**: 직접 거절 어려움 (보류 표현)
- **한국 비즈니스**: 정중 거절 = "검토 중"
- **명확한 시간 명시**: 보류 시 응답 시간 명시
- **일본어 "検討します (Kentō shimasu)"**와 일치

### Sources

- `[[Language/wiki/comparative/politeness-honorifics]]`

---

## 알겠습니다

**Part of Speech:** expression (acknowledgment)
**Definition:** "Understood" — 정중한 동의/수락.
**Form:** Algesseumnida.

### Usage

상사/고객의 지시 수락, 이메일/문자 응답.

### Variations

- **알겠습니다 (Algesseumnida)** — "Understood" (default 격식)
- **알았어요 (Alasseoyo)** — 캐주얼
- **알았어 (Alasseo)** — 매우 캐주얼
- **네, 알겠습니다 (Ne, algesseumnida)** — "Yes, understood"
- **충분히 알겠습니다 (Chungbunhi algesseumnida)** — "Understood thoroughly" (강조)

### Sample Sentences

- **네, 알겠습니다 (Ne, algesseumnida)** — "Yes, understood"
- **말씀하신 내용 잘 알겠습니다 (Malsseum hasin naeyong jal algesseumnida)** — "I understand what you said well"

### Cultural Notes

- **상사**: "알겠습니다" 정중
- **동료**: "알겠어" / "ㅇㅇ (응)" 캐주얼
- **카톡/문자**: "넵 (nep)" = 젊은 세대 "네"
- **일본어 "承知しました"**와 일치

### Sources

- `[[Language/wiki/comparative/politeness-honorifics]]`

---

## 죄송하지만

**Part of Speech:** expression (apology, polite transition)
**Definition:** "I'm sorry but..." — 부드러운 거절/중단 표현.
**Form:** Joesonghajiman.

### Usage

요청 거절, 대화 중단, 부정 답변.

### Variations

- **죄송하지만 (Joesonghajiman)** — "I'm sorry but" (default)
- **죄송합니다만 (Joesonghamnidaman)** — 같은 의미 (격식)
- **죄송합니다 (Joesonghamnida)** — 사과만
- **죄송한데요 (Joesonghandeyo)** — 캐주얼
- **미안한데 (Mianhande)** — "Sorry but" (캐주얼)

### Sample Sentences

- **죄송하지만, 참석이 어렵습니다 (Joesonghajiman, chamseogi eoryeopseumnida)** — "Sorry, attendance is difficult"
- **죄송하지만, 그건 어렵습니다 (Joesonghajiman, geugeon eoryeopseumnida)** — "Sorry, that's difficult"

### Cultural Notes

- **정중 거절**: "죄송하지만" = 부드러운 거절
- **실제 거절**: "그건 어렵습니다" / "상황이 어렵습니다" / "검토하겠습니다"
- **한국 문화**: 직접 거절 = 무례, 간접 = 정중
- **일본어 "申し訳ございません"**와 일치

### Sources

- `[[Language/wiki/comparative/politeness-honorifics]]`

---

## 확인 부탁드립니다

**Part of Speech:** expression (request, business)
**Definition:** "Please confirm" — 비즈니스 확인 요청.
**Form:** Hwagin butak deurimnida.

### Usage

이메일, 문서 검토, 사실 확인.

### Variations

- **확인 부탁드립니다 (Hwagin butak deurimnida)** — "Please confirm" (default)
- **확인 부탁해요 (Hwagin butakhaeyo)** — 정중
- **확인 부탁 (Hwagin butak)** — 캐주얼
- **확인 부탁드립니다만 (Hwagin butak deurimnidaman)** — 매우 정중

### Sample Sentences

- **일정 확인 부탁드립니다 (Iljeong hwagin butak deurimnida)** — "Please confirm the schedule"
- **첨부파일 확인 부탁드립니다 (Cheombupail hwagin butak deurimnida)** — "Please confirm the attached file"

### Cultural Notes

- **이메일**: "확인 부탁드립니다" + "감사합니다"
- **상사/거래처**: 매우 정중한 표현
- **CC 포함**: 중요 메일은 CC 추가
- **일본어 "ご確認ください (gokakunin kudasai)"**와 일치

### Sources

- `[[Language/wiki/comparative/business-email]]`

---

## 연락 드리겠습니다

**Part of Speech:** expression (action)
**Definition:** "I'll contact you" — 후속 연락 약속.
**Form:** Yeollak deurigetseumnida.

### Usage

이메일/문자/전화로 후속 연락 약속.

### Variations

- **연락 드리겠습니다 (Yeollak deurigetseumnida)** — "I'll contact you" (default 격식)
- **다시 연락 드리겠습니다 (Dasi yeollak deurigetseumnida)** — "I'll contact you again"
- **곧 연락 드리겠습니다 (Got yeollak deurigetseumnida)** — "I'll contact you soon"
- **다음 주에 연락 드리겠습니다 (Daeum jue yeollak deurigetseumnida)** — "I'll contact you next week"

### Sample Sentences

- **검토 후 연락 드리겠습니다 (Geomto hu yeollak deurigetseumnida)** — "I'll contact you after review"
- **확인되는 대로 연락 드리겠습니다 (Hwagindoeneun daero yeollak deurigetseumnida)** — "I'll contact you once confirmed"

### Cultural Notes

- **시간 명시**: 명확한 응답 시간 명시
- **약속 후 실행**: 한국 문화는 약속 중요 (실행 필수)
- **지연 시**: 미리 연락 (정중)
- **일본어 "ご連絡いたします (go-renraku itashimasu)"**와 일치

### Sources

- `[[Language/wiki/comparative/business-email]]`

---

## Quick Reference Card: 10 Korean Business Phrases

| # | Korean | Romaja | English |

## 업무 단어 & 표현 (Business terms & expressions)

> **Note (2026-07-28)**: 4개 단일 표현 (수고하세요, 열공하세요, 요약, 죄송합니다만) 가 per-word `.md` 스텁에서 본 theme-file 로 통합됨. 이전 per-word 페이지 inbound link 는 모두 `''X''` italic 으로 변환.

### 수고하세요 (sugo-haseyo)

**Part of Speech:** 서술어 (polite acknowledgment of work)

**Definition:** "You've worked hard." — 직장/학교/서비스에서 마주칠 때 정중한 인사/인정 표현.

**Romaja:** sugo-haseyo

**Etymology:** 수고 (辛苦, 한자어 "effort/hardship") + 하 (verb) + 세요 (polite ending).

#### Examples

- 회의 수고하셨습니다. — Thank you for your work in the meeting. (formal closing)
- 오늘 현장 수고하셨어요. — Thank you for your work at the site today. (direct superior → subordinate)

#### Related Terms

- *수고해요* — same, casual/polite mix
- *고생했어요* — same meaning, more colloquial

#### Cultural Notes

- 회의/이메일/SMS 끝에 자주 등장 ("수고하셨습니다" = "thank you for your effort")
- 직장 동료끼리는 일상적, 거래처/상사에게는 격식 더 필요 (수고하셨습니다)
- 학생 → 선생님: "수고하셨습니다" (less common; usually 선생님 → 학생)

#### Sources

- [[business-vocabulary]]

---

### 열공하세요 (yeol-gong-haseyo)

**Part of Speech:** 서술어 (encouragement)

**Definition:** "Study/work hard." — 시험/자격증/작업 마감을 앞둔 사람에게 쓰는 격려 표현.

**Romaja:** yeol-gong-haseyo

**Etymology:** 열공 (熱功, 한자어 약어 "열심히 공부하다") + 하 + 세요. 신조어 (1990년대 이후 학생 문화에서 유래).

#### Examples

- 시험 기간 화이팅, 열공하세요! — Good luck on exams, study hard!
- 프로젝트 마감까지 일주일, 모두 열공합시다. — One week until project deadline, let's all work hard.

#### Related Terms

- *열공합시다* — let's all study/work hard (group exhortation)
- *화이팅* — fighting! (English loanword, similar encouragement)
- *파이팅* — variant pronunciation

#### Cultural Notes

- 학생·수험생 문화에서 광범위 사용
- 직장에서는 "열공하세요" 보다 "열심히 해 주세요" 또는 "마감 잘 부탁드립니다" 가 더 격식적
- 신조어이지만 표준어 등재 (열심히 공부하다의 약자)

#### Sources

- [[business-vocabulary]]

---

### 요약 (yoyak)

**Part of Speech:** 명사 (summary) / 동사 (to summarize)

**Definition:** Summary, recapitulation. 회의/보고서/발표 끝에 핵심만 압축한 요점 정리.

**Romaja:** yoyak

**Etymology:** 要約 (한자어, 日語 영향). 동사형: 요약하다 → 요약했어요 / 요약됩니다.

#### Examples

- 오늘 회의 내용을 3가지로 요약하겠습니다. — Let me summarize today's meeting in 3 points.
- 보고서 마지막 장은 결론 및 요약입니다. — The last chapter of the report is conclusion and summary.

#### Related Terms

- *요점* — key point
- *개요* — outline, abstract
- *정리* — 정리하다 (to organize/summarize, more casual)

#### Cultural Notes

비즈니스: 회의록 → 보고서 → 발표 의 흐름에서 "요약" 단계 필수. 5W1H 원칙 적용. 한국 비즈니스 문서는 일반적으로 본문 + 별도 "요약" 섹션 구조.

#### Sources

- [[business-vocabulary]]

---

### 죄송합니다만 (joesong-hamnida-man)

**Part of Speech:** 종속절 (formal apology connector)

**Definition:** "Excuse me / I'm sorry, but..." — 정중한 打斷 (interruption) 또는 요청 도입부.

**Romaja:** joesong-hamnida-man

**Etymology:** 죄송 (罪悚, 한자어 "guilt") + 합니다 (formal polite) + 만 ("but/however" connector).

#### Examples

- 죄송합니다만, 잠깐 시간 있으세요? — Excuse me, do you have a moment?
- 죄송합니다만 다시 한번 말씀해 주시겠어요? — Sorry, could you say that again?

#### Related Terms

- *실례합니다만* — Excuse me (formal, e.g., 회의 중)
- *방해해도 될까요* — May I interrupt?
- *죄송한데* — same, casual/contracted

#### Cultural Notes

- 회의/통화에서 본격적인 요청·打斷 전에 사용 → 한국 비즈니스 매너의 핵심
- "죄송합니다만" 의 함축 의미: "나는 이 요청이 당신에게 부담임을 안다" → 부담 경감 후속 발화 가능
- 너무 자주 사용 시 오히려 진정성 의문 → 정당한 경우에만

#### Sources

- [[business-vocabulary]]

---

## Sources

- `[[wiki/Korean/vocabulary/topik1-starter]]`
- `[[Language/wiki/comparative/business-email]]`
- `[[Language/wiki/comparative/politeness-honorifics]]`

# American Workplace Culture: Open Door and Small Talk

**Overview:** American workplace culture values direct communication, individualism, and casual relationship-building through open-door policies and informal small talk.

## Key Points

- **Open Door Policy**: Managers keep office doors open — signaling approachability. "My door is always open" = invite for questions/discussion.
- **First Names**: American workplaces use first names quickly, even for bosses. "Hi, Sarah" vs. "Director Smith." Titles used sparingly.
- **Small Talk**: Essential to American workplace culture. Topics:
  - Weather ("Beautiful day, isn't it?")
  - Weekend plans ("How was your weekend?")
  - Sports (American football, baseball — "Did you see the game?")
  - Family/kids (carefully — avoid controversial topics)
- **Topics to Avoid**: Religion, politics, money/salary, controversial social issues.
- **Networking (business cards era → LinkedIn)**:
  - **Small talk** before business
  - **Follow-up email** within 24 hours
  - **LinkedIn** — primary professional network
- **Feedback Culture**:
  - "Feedback is a gift" — common HR phrase
  - **360-degree reviews**: Feedback from peers, subordinates, supervisors
  - **Performance Improvement Plans (PIP)**: Formal warning for underperformers
- **Work Hours**:
  - 9-5 standard (often 9-6)
  - "Working from home" (WFH) common since 2020
  - **Vacation/PTO** (Paid Time Off): 10-20 days/year standard
  - **At-will employment**: Can be fired without cause (most states)
- **Office Hierarchies**:
  - **C-Suite**: CEO, CFO, COO, CTO, CMO
  - **VP (Vice President)**
  - **Director**
  - **Manager**
  - **Individual Contributor (IC)**

## Language Connections

- `open door` (Open door policy)
- `small talk` (Casual conversation)
- `first-name basis` (직장 내 호칭)
- `feedback` (피드백)
- `performance review` (인사 평가)
- `PTO` (Paid time off, 유급 휴가)
- `networking` (네트워킹)
- `small talk` (잡담)

## Sources

- [[english-workplace-culture]]

# English-Speaking Holidays & Celebrations

**Type:** culture, social-ritual, calendar
**Region:** US / UK / Canada / Australia / NZ

## Overview

English-speaking holiday culture blends religious (Christian) heritage, secular national holidays, immigrant influences, and increasingly commercial events. While Christmas and Thanksgiving dominate, each country has unique observances. This page complements `[[english-dating-culture]]`, `[[english-school-life]]`, and `[[american-cultural-values]]`.

## Major Annual Holidays

### Calendar View

| Date | US | UK | Canada | AU/NZ |
|------|----|----|----|----|
| **Jan 1** | New Year's Day | New Year's Day | New Year's Day | New Year's Day |
| **Jan 6** | Epiphany (12th Night) | Epiphany | Epiphany | — |

| **Mar/Apr** | Easter | Easter | Easter | Easter |

| **May 1** | — | Early May Bank Holiday | — | May Day |
| **2nd Sun May** | Mother's Day | Mother's Day | Mother's Day | Mother's Day |
| **Last Mon May** | Memorial Day | Spring Bank Holiday | Victoria Day | — |
| **3rd Sun Jun** | Father's Day | Father's Day | Father's Day | Father's Day |
| **Jul 1** | — | — | Canada Day | — |

| **Dec 24** | Christmas Eve | Christmas Eve | Christmas Eve | Christmas Eve |

| **Dec 31** | New Year's Eve | New Year's Eve | New Year's Eve | New Year's Eve |

---

## Major Holiday Descriptions

### New Year's Day (Jan 1)

**Universal English-speaking celebration** — First major holiday of the year.

| Country | Custom |
|---------|--------|
| **US** | Rose Bowl parade (Pasadena), Times Square ball drop |
| **UK** | Hogmanay (Scotland), London fireworks |
| **Canada** | Ice wine celebrations |
| **AU/NZ** | Summer (Southern Hemisphere!) — beach parties |

**Greeting**: "Happy New Year!"
**Resolutions**: Common to make promises about self-improvement

### Valentine's Day (Feb 14)

**Romantic holiday** — Most commercial after Christmas.

| Country | Tradition |
|---------|-----------|
| **US** | Cards, flowers (especially red roses), chocolates |
| **UK** | Anonymous cards (Victorian tradition) |
| **Canada** | Similar to US |
| **AU** | Similar to US |

**Cultural Notes**:
- School children exchange cards (often non-romantic)
- Adults: romantic dinners, gifts
- Galentine's Day (Feb 13) — female friendship
- **Anti-Valentine's Day** (Feb 14): single people gatherings

### St. Patrick's Day (Mar 17)

**Irish heritage celebration** — Big in US (especially Chicago), widespread in UK/Ireland.

| Country | Custom |
|---------|-----------|
| **US** | Parades, green beer, dyeing rivers (Chicago) |
| **UK** | More subdued, church services |
| **Canada** | Parades (Montreal largest) |
| **AU** | Pub celebrations |

**Cultural Notes**:
- Color: Green (wearing it = safe)
- Food: Corned beef, Irish stew
- Drink: Guinness, Irish coffee
- **Irish-American**: Huge celebration in US

### Easter (Mar/Apr)

**Christian holiday** — Movable date based on lunar calendar.

| Country | Tradition |
|---------|-----------|
| **US** | Easter egg hunt, Easter Bunny, church services |
| **UK** | Easter eggs, hot cross buns, bank holidays |
| **Canada** | Similar to US/UK |
| **AU** | Hot cross buns, Easter bilbies (not bunnies) |

**Date**: First Sunday after first full moon after spring equinox

### Mother's Day (2nd Sunday May)

**US holiday that spread worldwide** — Anna Jarvis founded in 1908.

| Country | Date |
|---------|------|
| **US/Canada/AU/NZ** | 2nd Sunday May |
| **UK** | Mothering Sunday (4th Sunday Lent) — different! |
| **International** | March 8 (in some countries) |

### Father's Day (3rd Sunday June)

**Complement to Mother's Day** — Founded 1910 in US.

| Country | Date |
|---------|------|
| **US/Canada/UK** | 3rd Sunday June |
| **AU/NZ** | 1st Sunday September (different!) |

### Independence Day (Jul 4 - US)

**Major US holiday** — 1776 Declaration of Independence.

| Activity | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| **Fireworks** | Massive displays nationwide |
| **BBQ** | Outdoor grilling (hot dogs, hamburgers) |
| **Parades** | Patriotic processions |
| **Beaches/Pools** | Summer holiday peak |
| **Apple Pie** | Traditional dessert |

**Cultural Significance**: Most patriotic US holiday

### Canada Day (Jul 1)

**Similar to US Independence Day** — 1867 Confederation.

| Activity | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| **Fireworks** | Across the country |
| **Parades** | Especially in Ottawa |
| **Poutine** | National dish |
| **Maple Leaf flags** | Patriotic display |

### Halloween (Oct 31)

**Trick-or-treat** — Now mostly US/Canada (UK/AU mixed).

| Country | Custom |
|---------|--------|
| **US** | Costumes, trick-or-treat, haunted houses |
| **Canada** | Similar to US |
| **UK** | Less commercialized, growing |
| **AU** | Growing commercial holiday |

**Vocabulary**:
- "Trick or treat!"
- "Happy Halloween!"
- Costume: What you're wearing
- Jack-o'-lantern: Carved pumpkin

### Thanksgiving (US - 4th Thu Nov)

**Major US holiday** — Pilgrim/Wampanoag harvest meal.

| Element | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Turkey** | Roasted bird (centerpiece) |
| **Stuffing** | Bread-based side dish |
| **Cranberry sauce** | Tart side |
| **Mashed potatoes** | Standard side |
| **Pumpkin pie** | Traditional dessert |
| **Family gathering** | Extended family dinner |

**Canadian Thanksgiving**: 2nd Monday October (earlier!)
**No British equivalent** (closest: Harvest Festival)

### Remembrance Day (Nov 11)

**WWI commemoration** — Commonwealth-wide.

| Country | Note |
|---------|------|
| **Canada** | "Remembrance Day" — major holiday |
| **UK** | "Remembrance Sunday" (closest Sunday) |
| **AU/NZ** | "Remembrance Day" |
| **US** | "Veterans Day" — slightly different emphasis |

**Symbol**: Red poppy worn

### Black Friday (Day after US Thanksgiving)

**Shopping phenomenon** — Major US commercial day.

| Aspect | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **Origin** | Philadelphia police term (1960s) |
| **Expansion** | Big-box retail sales (1990s+) |
| **Modern** | Online + in-store, starts Thanksgiving evening |
| **Cyber Monday** | Online equivalent (Monday after) |

### Christmas (Dec 25)

**Major Christian/cultural holiday** — Widely secular in English-speaking countries.

| Country | Tradition |
|---------|-----------|
| **US** | Santa Claus, gifts, Christmas tree, family dinner |
| **UK** | Christmas crackers, Father Christmas, Boxing Day |
| **Canada** | Mixed US/UK traditions |
| **AU/NZ** | Summer Christmas! (25°C+), BBQ on beach |

**Vocabulary**:
- "Merry Christmas!" — standard greeting
- "Happy Holidays!" — more inclusive
- Santa Claus / Father Christmas / St. Nicholas
- Stockings (hung by fireplace)
- Mistletoe (kiss tradition)

### Boxing Day (Dec 26)

**British-origin holiday** — Day after Christmas.

| Country | Practice |
|---------|----------|
| **UK** | Boxing (sport), sales (shopping), bank holiday |
| **Canada** | Statutory holiday |
| **AU** | Public holiday (Proclamation Day) |
| **US** | Not observed (no holiday) |

**Origin**: Alms boxes, servants' day off, or hunting day

---

## Religious Holidays

### Christian Holidays

| Holiday | Date | Significance |
|---------|------|--------------|
| **Christmas** | Dec 25 | Birth of Jesus |
| **Easter** | Mar/Apr (movable) | Resurrection of Jesus |
| **Good Friday** | 2 days before Easter | Crucifixion |
| **Pentecost** | 50 days after Easter | Holy Spirit |
| **Ascension** | 40 days after Easter | Jesus ascends to heaven |
| **Assumption** | Aug 15 | Mary's assumption to heaven |
| **All Saints' Day** | Nov 1 | Saints honored |
| **All Souls' Day** | Nov 2 | Dead remembered |

### Secular Holidays

✅ **Try holiday foods** — Cultural participation
✅ **Bring appropriate gifts** — Wine, flowers, chocolates (alcohol alternatives)
✅ **Respect religious restrictions** — Halal, Kosher, vegetarian

### What to Avoid

❌ **Don't assume everyone celebrates Christmas** — Many don't
❌ **Don't wish "Merry Christmas" only** — Add "Happy Holidays" for inclusivity
❌ **Don't criticize religious holidays** — Sensitive topic
❌ **Don't impose your holiday on others** — "Office Christmas party" may exclude
❌ **Don't use religious holidays for marketing** — Backlash possible
❌ **Don't ask intrusive questions** — "Why don't you celebrate?" can be rude

# American Food Culture: Thanksgiving and Regional Cuisines

**Overview:** American cuisine is a melting pot of immigrant traditions, with regional specialties reflecting historical settlement patterns and local ingredients.

## Key Points

- **Thanksgiving Dinner (4th Thursday of November)**:
  - **Turkey (七面鳥)**: Centerpiece — often 12-20 lbs, stuffed with bread stuffing
  - **Mashed Potatoes (マッシュポテト)**: With gravy
  - **Stuffing (スタッフィング)**: Bread-based, with herbs (sage, thyme)
  - **Cranberry Sauce (クランベリーソース)**: Sweet-tart condiment
  - **Sweet Potato Casserole (スイートポテト)**: Often with marshmallows on top
  - **Pumpkin Pie (パンプキンパイ)**: Traditional dessert — Thanksgiving-specific
  - **Gravy (グレイビー)**: From turkey drippings
  - **Mac and Cheese (マックアンドチーズ)**: Especially Southern
- **Regional Cuisines**:
  - **Southern (BBQ, Cajun/Creole, Low Country)**: BBQ sauces (vinegar-based NC, mustard SC, tomato-based KC, sweet Memphis), gumbo, jambalaya, shrimp & grits
  - **Tex-Mex (Texas, Southwest)**: Chili con carne, fajitas, breakfast tacos
  - **New England (Lobster, Clam Chowder)**: Boston cream pie, lobster rolls
  - **Midwest (Chicago, Detroit)**: Deep-dish pizza, coney dogs
  - **California Cuisine**: Fusion, farm-to-table
  - **Pacific Northwest**: Salmon, coffee culture (Seattle/Portland)
- **Fast Food Culture**:
  - McDonald's, Burger King, Wendy's, Taco Bell
  - Drive-thru (order without leaving car)
- **Casseroles and Comfort Food**: Mac and cheese, pot pie, meatloaf
- **Regional BBQ Differences**:
  - **Texas**: Beef brisket, dry rub
  - **Memphis**: Pork ribs, dry rub OR wet sauce
  - **Kansas City**: Burnt ends, sweet thick sauce
  - **North Carolina**: Whole hog, vinegar-based sauce
  - **South Carolina**: Mustard-based yellow sauce

## Language Connections

- `Thanksgiving` (4th Thursday in November)
- `Black Friday` (Day after Thanksgiving)
- `Turkey` (鳥肉, 七面鳥)
- `Pumpkin pie` (パンプキンパイ)
- `BBQ` (バーベキュー)
- `Soul food` (Southern cuisine)
- `Casserole` (キャセロール)
- `Drive-thru` (ドライブスルー)

- [[english-holidays]]
- [[english-holidays]]

english-dating-culture.md.title: English Dating Culture
english-dating-culture.md.body:
# English Dating Culture

**Type:** romance, social-ritual
**Region:** US / UK / Canada / Australia (English-speaking countries)

## Overview

English-speaking countries (especially US) have **explicit, individualist** dating culture. Romantic intent is usually stated clearly, consent is verbal, and personal boundaries are respected. Modern dating emphasizes direct communication, gender equality (in principle), and emotional honesty.

## Setting

A first date in the US/UK: **coffee shop, restaurant, bar, or walk in a park**. Evening (7-9pm typical). Casual to smart-casual dress. Two people meeting with romantic intent, getting to know each other.

## Roles

- **Person who invites (inviter)** — takes initiative, suggests time/place
- **Invitee** — can accept, suggest alternatives, or decline politely
- Both pay attention to comfort, consent, and clear communication

## Scenario: A Typical First Date

1. **Planning** — Inviter suggests a specific time/place ("Want to grab coffee Saturday at 3?")
2. **Acceptance** — Invitee confirms or reschedules
3. **Arrival** — Both arrive on time (5 min early is normal); greet with smile + light hug or wave
4. **Conversation** — Mix of light (hobbies, work) and deeper (values, life goals) topics
5. **Physical contact** — Wait for clear signals; ask before initiating hand-holding or kissing
6. **Bill** — Often offered by inviter, but splitting is normal; "Let's split?" is OK
7. **End** — Confirm interest: "I had a great time, want to do this again?"
8. **Follow-up text** — Within 24 hours: "Thanks for tonight, I really enjoyed it."

## Cultural Insight

### "Hanging Out" vs "Dating"

In US English, "date" implies **explicit romantic intent**. "Hang out" is ambiguous — could be friends or romantic. Modern dating advice encourages **clarifying intent early** to avoid misunderstandings.

**"Are we hanging out or dating?"** is a real conversation that happens. Best to be clear from the start.

### Splitting the Bill

**Generation gap**:
- Older generations: man traditionally pays
- Younger (Z, Millennials): 50/50 split is normal
- Most common: person who invited pays, but offering to split is polite

**Tactful**: Don't insist either way. "Let's split it?" or "I've got this one" are both fine.

### Consent Culture

Modern English-speaking countries (especially US/Canada/UK) have embraced **explicit verbal consent**:
- "Can I hold your hand?"
- "Can I kiss you?"
- "Is this okay?"

Not asking is now considered a **red flag**. Asking is **mature**, not awkward.

### "I Love You" Timing

- **US**: typically 2-3 months into a relationship
- **UK**: often later (3-6 months)
- **Australia**: relatively early (1-2 months)

Earlier expression: "I really like you" (more universally safe).

### Personal Space

- **Friends/acquaintances**: ~45cm (18in)
- **Romantic partners**: closer, touching common
- **Strangers**: arm's length+

**Eye contact**: 60-70% during conversation = interested.

### Online / Text Dating

- **Apps**: Tinder, Bumble, Hinge dominant in US/UK
- **First contact**: text/messaging common
- **Phone call**: more sincere, less common
- **Asking out**: text is fine; in-person or call for serious intent

## Useful Phrases

- i-like-you — early affection
- i-love-you — deep feeling
- beautiful — appearance compliment
- handsome — male appearance compliment
- kind — personality compliment
- can-i-kiss-you — consent request
- would-you-like-to — invitation
- i-had-a-great-time — end-of-date
- see-you-again — follow-up

## What NOT to Do

- ❌ **"Wanna date?"** in first message — too direct
- ❌ **Bombarding texts** — turn-off
- ❌ **"You up?"** late-night texts — usually means casual sex
- ❌ **Love bombing** — excessive flattery early
- ❌ **Ghosting** — disappearing without explanation (avoidable but common)
- ❌ **"You're so beautiful"** to a stranger on the street — catcalling, harassment
- ❌ **Asking weight, age, salary** on first date — too personal
- ❌ **Talking only about yourself** — reciprocal conversation expected

## Body Language

| Gesture | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Eye contact 60-70% | Interested, engaged |
| Mirroring (leaning in, gestures) | Comfortable, in sync |
| Looking at phone during date | Disinterested, rude |
| Fidgeting, looking around | Nervous or bored |
| Touching face/hair (other person) | Often flirting, but not always |
| Hand on table palm up | Inviting touch |
| Turning body toward you | Engaged |

## Cross-Reference

- Compare with: [[japanese-dating-culture]], [[spanish-dating-culture]], [[korean-dating-culture]]
- See also: i-love-you, beautiful, handsome

## Holiday / Special Days

- **Valentine's Day** (Feb 14) — big romantic holiday
- **Anniversaries** — celebrate relationship start
- **No formal "100 days" celebration** (unlike Korean culture)

## Examples

"Coffee date" — first-date archetype in US urban culture, neutral public setting.
"Hinge" (launched 2012) — dating app designed for "designed to be deleted" with relationship focus.
"Ghosting" — abruptly cutting off all communication without explanation, common post-2010s dating culture phenomenon.

---

## Sources

- [[dating-romance]] — main source
- BBC Learning English — Relationships
- The Atlantic — Modern dating essays
- OKCupid / Hinge dating blog posts
- Consent culture resources (Planned Parenthood, etc.)

# Movie Quotes (English)

**Source:** [[movie-quotes]]
**Theme:** Movies / Entertainment
**Level:** B1-C1 (Intermediate-Advanced)

Iconic lines from famous movies. Useful for cultural understanding, conversation practice, and learning natural English expressions through film dialogue.

---

## Famous Iconic Quotes

### "May the Force be with you."

**Source:** Star Wars (1977)

**Meaning:** 은하 제국의 팰퍼시트 (= 별의 전쟁) 시리즈

#### Vocabulary Breakdown

- Force — 힘, 힘 (초자연적 힘)
- be with you — 너와 함께하다

#### Cultural Impact

- 영화 역사상 가장 유명한 대사 중 하나
- AFI (American Film Institute) 100대 명대사 중 8위
- "Star Wars" 시리즈 전편에 등장

### "I'll be back."

**Source:** The Terminator (1984)

**Meaning:** 다시 돌아오겠다

#### Vocabulary Breakdown

- I'll — I will (축약형)
- be back — 돌아오다

#### Cultural Impact

- 아놀드 슈워제네거의 시그니처 대사
- AFI 100대 명대사 중 37위
- 속기 쉬운 짧고 임팩트 있는 대사

### "Here's looking at you, kid."

**Source:** Casablanca (1942)

**Meaning:** 너를 바라보고 있단다

#### Vocabulary Breakdown

- Here's — Here is (축약형)
- looking at — 바라보다
- kid — 아이, 젊은이

#### Cultural Impact

- 험프리 보가트의 대표 대사
- AFI 100대 명대사 1위
- "Casablanca" 의 상징적 장면

### "You can't handle the truth!"

**Source:** A Few Good Men (1992)

**Meaning:** 너는 진실을 감당할 수 없어!

#### Vocabulary Breakdown

- can't — cannot (축약형)
- handle — 다루다, 감당하다
- truth — 진실

### "Houston, we have a problem."

**Source:** Apollo 13 (1995)

**Meaning:** 휴스턴, 문제가 생겼습니다

#### Cultural Impact

- NASA 실제 사고에서 영감
- 영화 역사상 유명한 대사

## Famous Movie Genres

| English | Korean |
|---------|--------|
| Action | 액션 |
| Comedy | 코미디 |
| Drama | 드라마 |
| Horror | 호러 |
| Romance | 로맨스 |
| Sci-fi | 공상과학 |
| Fantasy | 판타지 |
| Thriller | 스릴러 |
| Animation | 애니메이션 |
| Documentary | 다큐멘터리 |

## Essential Movie Phrases

- "I'll be right back." — 곧 돌아오겠습니다
- "This is it." — 이게 시작이다
- "Don't look back." — 뒤를 돌아보지 마라
- "I'm coming for you." — 너를 찾아가겠다
- "We'll see about that." — 그건 두고 봐야 알겠지
- "Time is running out." — 시간이 얼마 안 남았다
- "I knew it!" — 역시!

## Cultural Notes

- AFI (American Film Institute) 100대 명대사 - 미국 영화 명대사 순위
- IMDb (Internet Movie Database) - 영화/TV 정보 사이트
- 한국 영화: 봉준호, 박찬욱 등 세계적 감독
- 영화 대사 학습 = 회화 표현 + 문화 이해
- 명대사 암기 = 영어 회화 실력 향상

## Sources

- AFI's 100 Years...100 Movie Quotes
- Various movie scripts and transcripts
- IMDb Top Quotes

## Pronunciation Notes

| Pattern | Example | Korean Learner Tip |
|---------|---------|-------------------|
| th sound | the, this | Tongue between teeth → /θ/ |
| r sound | really, recognize | Tongue curled back → /ɹ/ |
| schwa | problem, different | Very short /ə/ |
| -ing ending | looking, running | /ɪŋ/ sound, Korean ㅇ |
| -ed ending | wanted, looked | /ɪd/, /d/, /t/ depending on sound |

# English-Speaking School Culture

**Type:** culture, education, social-norms
**Region:** US / UK / Canada / Australia / NZ

## Overview

English-speaking school culture emphasizes individualism, Socratic discussion, extracurricular activities, and preparing for college admission. The US system differs significantly from UK (more formal), Canadian (similar to US), and Australian/NZ (more casual, less competitive). This page complements `[[english-dating-culture]]`, `[[english-workplace-culture]]`, and `[[american-cultural-values]]`.

## School System Comparison

### Educational Stages

| Stage | Age (approx) | US | UK | Canada | AU |
|-------|-------------|----|----|----|----|
| Pre-K / Reception | 3-5 | Pre-K / Kindergarten | Reception | Junior Kindergarten | Pre-School |
| Elementary / Primary | 5-11 | Elementary (K-5) | Primary (Y1-Y6) | Elementary (K-6) | Primary (K-6) |
| Middle | 11-14 | Middle School (6-8) | — | Middle School (7-9) | — |
| High / Secondary | 14-18 | High School (9-12) | Secondary (Y7-Y13) | Secondary (9-12) | Secondary (7-12) |
| Sixth Form | 16-18 | — | Sixth Form College | — | Year 11-12 |
| University | 18-22 | College / University | University | University | University |

### School Year

| Country | Year Start | Year End |
|---------|------------|-----------|
| **US** | Late August / September | Late May / June |
| **UK** | September | July |
| **Canada** | September | June |
| **AU/NZ** | January / February | November / December |

### School Day Times

| Country | Start | End | Total |
|---------|-------|-----|-------|
| **US (HS)** | 7:30-8:30 AM | 2:30-3:30 PM | 6.5-7 hrs |
| **UK (Sec)** | 8:30-9:00 AM | 3:00-3:30 PM | 6.5 hrs |
| **Canada** | 8:30-9:00 AM | 3:00-3:30 PM | 6 hrs |
| **AU (Sec)** | 8:30-9:00 AM | 3:00-3:30 PM | 6.5 hrs |

---

## Academic Culture

### Class Discussion

| Behavior | US | UK | Canada | AU |
|---------|----|----|----|----|
| Speak up in class | Expected | Encouraged | Expected | Expected |
| Question the teacher | Common | Acceptable | Common | Common |
| Group projects | Standard | Standard | Standard | Standard |
| Socratic method | Common | Common | Common | Less common |
| Call teacher by first name | Common | Rare | Common | Common |

### Grading System

| Country | Scale | "A" Equivalent |
|---------|-------|---------------|
| **US (GPA)** | 0.0-4.0 | 4.0 = A (90-100%) |
| **US (Letter)** | A-F | A+ (97-100) |
| **UK (A-Levels)** | A*-U | A* (90-100%) |
| **UK (GCSE)** | 9-1 | 9 (90-100%) |
| **Canada** | 0-100 | 80+ = A |
| **AU (ATAR)** | 0-99.95 | 99+ (top) |

### College Entrance Exams

| Country | Test | Format | Frequency |
|---------|-------|--------|-----------|
| **US** | SAT / ACT | Multiple choice | Multiple times/year |
| **UK** | A-Levels | Subject-specific | Once (Y13) |
| **Canada** | SAT (similar to US) | Multiple choice | Multiple |
| **AU** | ATAR / HSC / VCE | Subject-specific | Once (Y12) |

---

## School Vocabulary

### People

| EN | Age Range | Notes |
|----|-----------|-------|
| Preschooler | 3-5 | Pre-K |
| Kindergartener | 5-6 | First year of school |
| Elementary schooler | 6-11 | Grades K-5 |
| Middle schooler | 11-14 | Grades 6-8 |
| High schooler | 14-18 | Grades 9-12 |
| Freshman | 14-15 | First year HS |
| Sophomore | 15-16 | Second year HS |
| Junior | 16-17 | Third year HS |
| Senior | 17-18 | Fourth year HS |
| Freshman (college) | 18-19 | First year uni |
| Sophomore | 19-20 | Second year uni |
| Junior | 20-21 | Third year uni |
| Senior | 21-22 | Fourth year uni |

### Places

| EN | Context |
|----|---------|
| Classroom | Standard learning space |
| Lecture hall | College (US) / Uni (UK) |
| Auditorium | All-school assembly space |
| Cafeteria | Where students eat |
| Library | Study / research space |
| Gymnasium | Sports / PE class |
| Hallway | Common transit area |
| Faculty | Teachers' lounge (US) |
| Staff room | Teachers' lounge (UK) |
| Quidditch pitch | Harry Potter only 😉 |

### Supplies

| EN | Description |
|----|-------------|
| Backpack | Standard carry-all |
| Lunch box / Lunch pail | Carries meal |
| Pencil case | Holds writing tools |
| Eraser | Mistakes happen |
| Notebook / Binder | Lecture notes |
| Textbook | Course material |
| Laptop | Modern standard |
| Calculator | Math courses |
| Highlighter | Note-taking |
| Flash drive | File sharing |
| Thumb drive | Same |

---

## School Subjects

| EN | US | UK | Australia |
|----|----|----|-----------|
| **Math** | Math / Algebra / Geometry / Calculus | Mathematics | Mathematics |
| **Science** | Biology, Chemistry, Physics | Combined Science / Separate Sciences | Science |
| **English** | English / Literature | English Literature | English |
| **History** | US History / World History | History | History |
| **Geography** | Geography | Geography | Geography |
| **PE** | Physical Education (PE) | PE / Games | Health & PE |
| **Music** | Band / Choir / Orchestra | Music | Music |
| **Art** | Art | Art | Visual Arts |
| **Drama** | Drama / Theater | Drama | Drama |
| **Computer** | Computer Science / Technology | ICT (Information & Communication Technology) | Digital Technologies |

---

## High School Experience

### American High School

- **Sports culture**: Football (fall), basketball (winter), baseball/track (spring)
- **Prom** (Junior + Senior)
- **Homecoming** (fall)
- **Graduation** (ceremony + parties)
- **Yearbook**
- **Clubs**: 50+ typical (chess club, robotics, drama, etc.)
- **Lunch**: 30 min, cafeteria or off-campus
- **AP (Advanced Placement) courses**: College credit possible
- **SAT/ACT**: Junior year (optional but important)
- **Extracurriculars**: Critical for college applications
- **Spirit week, homecoming, prom**: Major events

### British High School

- **Sixth Form College** (Y12-Y13): Specialized A-Levels
- **A-Levels**: Subject-specific exams (3-4 subjects)
- **UCAS application**: For university admission
- **House system**: Common (Harry Potter-esque)
- **School uniform**: Standard (formal)
- **Sports**: Rugby, cricket, football (soccer)
- **Formal dinners, speech days**: Major events

### Canadian High School

- Similar to US system
- **Provincial variations** (Ontario, Quebec, BC, Alberta differ)
- **Quebec**: French-language schools (CÉGEP)
- **Sports**: Hockey (Canada's national sport!)
- **Co-op programs**: Work-integrated learning
- **Provincial exams** (varies)

### Australian High School

- **Less competitive** than US/Asia
- **ATAR**: University admission (state-specific)
- **Year 12 final exams**: Major event
- **Schoolies week**: Post-grad celebration
- **Sports**: AFL, cricket, rugby, NRL
- **Uniforms**: Standard (often distinctive colors)
- **Casual, friendly culture**: Less hierarchical than UK

---

## College/University Culture

### American College

- **Dorm life**: Freshman dorms, Greek life
- **Majors**: Declared sophomore year
- **Gen-Ed requirements**: First 2 years
- **Semester system**: Fall/Spring (+ optional Summer)
- **Tuition**: Very high ($30-70K/year private)
- **Sports culture**: NCAA, football Saturdays
- **Greek life (fraternities/sororities)**: Common but controversial

### British University

- **Halls of residence**: First year accommodation
- **Subject-focused**: Apply directly to course
- **3-year undergraduate** (typical, vs. US 4-year)
- **Tutorial system**: Oxford/Cambridge famous
- **Term system**: Michaelmas, Hilary, Trinity (Oxford)
- **Pub culture**: Central to social life
- **Tuition**: £9,250/year (capped for UK students)

### Canadian University

- Similar to US system but cheaper
- **Co-op programs**: Common (work + study)
- **U15 (top universities)**: Toronto, UBC, McGill, etc.
- **French immersion** (Quebec)
- **Undergraduate 4 years** (most programs)

### Australian University

- **3-year undergraduate** (typical)
- **Sandstone universities**: Oldest, prestigious (Melbourne, Sydney)
- **Group of Eight**: Top research universities
- **ATAR-based admission**: Similar to UK
- **Residential colleges**: On-campus accommodation
- **Pub culture**: Very strong (uni bars)
- **Casual, outdoorsy culture**: Less formal than UK

---

## Vocabulary by Activity

### Studying

| EN | Meaning |
|----|---------|
| "Study for an exam" | Prepare for test |
| "Cram" | Last-minute study |
| "Pull an all-nighter" | Study through the night |
| "Cheat sheet / crib sheet" | Illegal notes used in exam |
| "Cheat" | Use unauthorized help in exam |
| "Office hours" | Professor availability time |
| "TA (Teaching Assistant)" | Graduate student instructor |
| "Professor / Lecturer" | Senior teacher |
| "Thesis / Dissertation" | Long research paper |
| "GPA" | Grade Point Average |
| "Dean's List" | Academic honor |
| "Major / Minor" | Primary/secondary field |
| "Drop a class" | Withdraw from course |
| "Audit a class" | Take without credit |
| "Pass/Fail" | Alternative grading |

### School Events

| EN | Description |
|----|-------------|
| **Orientation** | Welcome new students |
| **Freshman Week / Welcome Week** | First week activities |
| **Homecoming** | Alumni return celebration |
| **Prom** | Formal dance (US HS/college) |
| **Graduation** | End-of-program ceremony |
| **Alumni reunion** | Past students gather |
| **Talent show** | Performance event |
| **Sports game/match** | Athletic competition |

| **Assembly** | All-school gathering |

---

## Cultural Concepts (Unique to English-speaking schools)

| Concept | Definition | Country |
|---------|------------|---------|
| **Ivy League** | 8 elite US universities | US |
| **Oxbridge** | Oxford + Cambridge | UK |
| **Sandstone universities** | Oldest Australian universities (Melbourne, Sydney) | Australia |
| **Russell Group** | 24 top UK research universities | UK |
| **Ivy Plus / Hidden Ivies** | Elite universities outside Ivy League | US |
| **Junior year abroad** | US study-abroad tradition | US |
| **Gap year** | Year off before university | UK/AU |
| **Hogwarts houses** | School house system (and inspiration) | UK/movies |
| **Study hall** | Supervised study period | US |
| **Detention** | After-school punishment | US/UK |

### Famous Fictional Schools (Pop Culture)

| School | Source | Country Equivalent |
|--------|---------|-------------------|
| **Hogwarts** | Harry Potter | UK public school |
| **Beverly Hills High** | Clueless | US elite school |
| **Rydell High** | Grease | US 1950s |
| **East High** | High School Musical | US modern |
| **McKinley High** | Glee | US modern |
| **Shermer** | Breakfast Club | US suburban |

---

## Academic Concepts

| EN | Meaning |
|----|---------|
| **GPA** | Grade Point Average (0.0-4.0) |
| **SAT** | Scholastic Assessment Test |
| **ACT** | American College Testing |
| **GPA** | Grade Point Average |
| **AP** | Advanced Placement (college credit) |
| **IB** | International Baccalaureate |
| **Honors** | Advanced-level courses |
| **Dean** | Head of school/college |
| **Provost** | Senior academic administrator |
| **Chancellor** | Head of university system |
| **Tenure** | Permanent faculty position |
| **Sabbatical** | Paid research leave |
| **Dissertation** | Doctoral research paper |
| **Thesis** | Master's research paper |

### "Cram" Culture

| EN | Meaning |
|----|---------|
| "Pull an all-nighter" | Study through the night |
| "Cram session" | Intense study session |
| "Memorize" | Rote learning |
| "Flash cards" | Quick study cards |
| "Cheat sheet" | (Illegal) hidden notes |
| "Senioritis" | Senior year laziness |
| "Brain freeze" | Mental block during test |
| "Go blank" | Mind goes empty |
| "Test anxiety" | Stress before/during exam |

---

## Cultural Tips for Visitors

✅ **Ask about school culture** — Will engage in conversation
✅ **Participate in student activities** — Sports, clubs
✅ **Use "How was school?"** as small talk
✅ **Respect homework culture** — Children are busy
✅ **Try cafeteria food** — Cultural experience
✅ **Attend sports events** — Social bonding

❌ **Don't criticize US testing culture** — Sensitive topic
❌ **Don't ask about college debt** — Common pain point
❌ **Don't assume all schools are same** — US vs UK very different
❌ **Don't ignore dress codes** — Some schools strict
❌ **Don't skip graduation ceremonies** — Important family event

## Examples

SAT (Scholastic Assessment Test, since 1926) — college admissions standardized test, scoring 400-1600 per section.
Homecoming — annual autumn tradition since early 20th century, with football game + dance + alumni events.
Spring Break — week-long recess in March/April, popular Florida/Mexico destinations, beach-focused culture.

# Health (건강) - Korean Translation

이 페이지는 한국인이 일본어 의료·건강 어휘를 학습할 때 사용하는 한국어 관점 참고 자료입니다. 의료施設 (病院/医者/薬局) + 약 (薬) + 증상 (頭痛/熱/風邪) + 신체部位 (頭/胃) + 예약 (予約) 을 다룹니다. 각 단어의 한국어 정의, 발음 (히라가나/로마자), 한자 어원, 한국어 예문, 한국·일본 의료 문화 비교를 포함합니다.

**참고:** 본 페이지는 `wiki/Japanese/vocabulary/health-vocabulary.md` 의 한국어 번역/관점 페이지 입니다. 일본어 원문 표제(見出し)는 한자 + 히라가나(讀み方) 형식으로 표기.

---

## 의료시설 (Medical Facilities)

### 病院 (びょういん)

**품사:** 명사 (noun)

**정의:** 병원 — 종합병원. 한국어 "병원" / 한자어 "병원(病院)" 와 의미 동일.

**読み方 (읽는 法):** びょういん (히라가나) / byouin (로마자) / 病院 (한자, 音読み: びょういん byouin)

**IPA / 발음:** /bjoː.in/

**어원:** 漢字 "病" (음읽 びょう/へい, 訓읽 や.む/やまい) + "院" (음읽 いん, 訓읽 いん). 한국어 한자어 "병원(病院)" 동일 한자, 한국어 역음 "병원". 어원: 病 = 병, 院 = 건물/원.

#### 예문

- **病院**は駅の近くです。 — 병원은 역 근처입니다. (위치, 격식)
- **病院**に行きます。 — 병원에 갑니다. (방문, 캐주얼)
- 大きい**病院**で働いています。 — 큰 병원에서 일합니다. (직장, 격식)

#### 관련 용어

- 病院 (びょういん) — 「병원 (종합)」
- 医院 (いいん) — 「의원 (개인)」
- 診療所 (しんりょうしょ) — 「진료소 (소형)」
- 救急病院 (きゅうきゅうびょういん) — 「응급 병원」
- [[health-vocabulary]] — 건강 어휘

#### 문화적 맥락

일본어 **病院 (びょういん)** 발음 "뵤인" — 한국어 "병원" (한자어) 와 발음 유사. 캐주얼: 病院 / 격식: 総合病院 (そうごうびょういん). 한국어 "병원" + "의원" / "한의원" / "한방병원" 의 어원 비교. 일본 의료체계: **保険証 (ほけんしょう, 건강보험증)** 필수 — 한국어 "건강보험증" 동일. 발음: びょういん (byo-u-in) — 한국어 ㅂ + ㅇ + ㄴ 발음 연습.

#### 출처

- [[health-vocabulary]]

---

### 医者 (いしゃ)

**품사:** 명사 (noun)

**정의:** 의사 — 의학 전문가. 한국어 "의사" / 한자어 "의사(醫者)" 의미.

**読み方 (읽는 법):** いしゃ (히라가나) / isha (로마자) / 医者 (한자, 音読み: いしゃ isha)

**IPA / 발음:** /i.ɕa/

**어원:** 漢字 "醫" (음읽 い, 訓읽 い.やす/い.する) + "者" (음읽 しゃ, 訓읽 もの). 한국어 한자어 "의자(醫者)" 의미. 어원: 醫 = 의술, 者 = 사람.

#### 예문

- **医者**に診てもらう必要があります。 — 의사에게 진료를 받아야 할 필요가 있습니다. (치료, 격식)
- **医者**になりたいです。 — 의사가 되고 싶습니다. (직업, 캐주얼)
- **医者**は土曜日も働きます。 — 의사는 토요일에도 일합니다. (근무, 격식)

#### 관련 용어

- 医者 (いしゃ) — 「의사 (일반)」
- 医師 (いし) — 「의사 (격식)」
- 内科医 (ないかい) — 「내과 의사」
- 外科医 (げかい) — 「외과 의사」
- [[health-vocabulary]] — 건강 어휘

#### 문화적 맥락

일본어 **医者 (いしゃ)** 발음 "이샤" — 한국어 "이샤" (伊射) 와 발음 동일. 캐주얼: 医者 / 격식: 医師 (いし). 한국어 "의사" + "한의사" (韓醫師) 의 어원 비교. 일본 **医師 (いし)** 의 국가시험 (医師国家試験) — 한국 "의사 국가시험" 동일. **お医者さん (おいしゃさん)** = 존칭. 발음: いしゃ (i-sha) — 한국어 ㅇ + ㅅ 발음 연습.

#### 출처

- [[health-vocabulary]]

---

### 薬局 (やっきょく)

**품사:** 명사 (noun)

**정의:** 약국 — 약을 파는 곳. 한국어 "약국" / 한자어 "약국(藥局)" 의미.

**読み方 (읽는 법):** やっきょく (히라가나) / yakkyoku (로마자) / 薬局 (한자, 音読み: やっきょく yakkyoku)

**IPA / 발음:** /jak.kjok.kɯ/

**어원:** 漢字 "藥" (음읽 やく, 訓읽 くすり) + "局" (음읽 きょく, 訓읽 つま/つぼね). 한국어 한자어 "약국(藥局)" 동일 한자, 한국어 역음 "약국". 어원: 藥 = 약, 局 = 관청/국.

#### 예문

- **薬局**は遅くまで開いています。 — 약국은 늦게까지 열려 있습니다. (영업시간, 격식)
- **薬局**で薬を買います。 — 약국에서 약을 삽니다. (구매, 캐주얼)
- 近くの**薬局**はどこですか? — 근처 약국은 어디입니까? (위치, 격식)

#### 관련 용어

- 薬局 (やっきょく) — 「약국 (의약품)」
- ドラッグストア (doraggu sutoa) — 「드럭스토어 (생활용품 + 약)」
- 処方箋 (しょほうせん) — 「처방전」
- 薬剤師 (やくざいし) — 「약사」
- [[health-vocabulary]] — 건강 어휘

#### 문화적 맥락

일본어 **薬局 (やっきょく)** 발음 "약쿄쿠" — 한국어 "약국" (한자어) 와 발음 유사. 캐주얼: 薬局 (yak-kyo-ku) / 약자: 薬屋 (くすりや). 한국어 "약국" 동일. 일본 **薬局** vs **ドラッグストア (드럭스토어)** — 한국어 "약국" vs "올리브영" 의 구분. 일본 **処方箋 (しょほうせん, 처방전)** = 한국어 "처방전" 동일. 발음: やっきょく (ya-kkyo-ku) — 촉음 っ + ㄲ + ㅋ 발음 연습.

#### 출처

- [[health-vocabulary]]

---

## 약 (Medicine)

### 薬 (くすり)

**품사:** 명사 (noun)

**정의:** 약 — 의약품. 한국어 "약" 의미.

**読み方 (읽는 법):** くすり (히라가나) / kusuri (로마자) / 薬 (한자, 音読み: やく yaku, 訓読み: くすり kusuri)

**IPA / 발음:** /kɯ.sɯ.ɾi/

**어원:** 漢字 "藥" (음읽 やく, 訓읽 くすり). 한국어 한자어 "약(藥)" 의미. 어원: 艹 (초) + 楽 (풍류) → 풀거름 약초 → 약.

#### 예문

- この**薬**を一日二回飲んでください。 — 이 약을 하루 두 번 드세요. (복용, 격식)
- **薬**は水と一緒に飲んでください。 — 약은 물과 함께 드세요. (복용, 격식)
- **薬**が効きます。 — 약이 듣습니다. (효과, 캐주얼)

#### 관련 용어

- 薬 (くすり) — 「약 (캐주얼)」
- 薬 (くすり) — 「약 (의약품)」
- 飲み薬 (のみぐすり) — 「먹는 약」
- 塗り薬 (ぬりぐすり) — 「바르는 약」
- 薬 (yaku) — 「약 (음읽, 한자어)」
- [[health-vocabulary]] — 건강 어휘

#### 문화적 맥락

일본어 **薬 (くすり)** 발음 "쿠스리" — 한국어 "쿠스리" (クスリ) 와 발음 동일. 캐주얼: くすり / 음읽: 薬 (やく). 한국어 "약" / 한자어 "약" (약) 동일. 일용어: **薬缶 (やかん, 주전자)** = "물주전자" (薬 약 缶 통) — 한국어 "주전자" 와 어원이 다름. **飲む (nomu, 마시다)** = 한국어 "마시다" (음료) / "드시다" (약). 발음: くすり (ku-su-ri) — 한국어 ㅅ + ㄹ 발음 연습.

#### 출처

- [[health-vocabulary]]

---

## 증상 (Symptoms)

### 頭痛 (ずつう)

**품사:** 명사 (noun)

**정의:** 두통 — 머리 통증. 한국어 "두통" / 한자어 "두통(頭痛)" 의미.

**読み方 (읽는 法):** ずつう (히라가나) / zutsuu (로마자) / 頭痛 (한자, 音読み: ずつう zutsuu)

**IPA / 발음:** /zɯt.tsɯː/

**어원:** 漢字 "頭" (음읽 とう/ず, 訓읽 あたま/かしら) + "痛" (음읽 つう, 訓읽 いた.い/いた.む). 한국어 한자어 "두통(頭痛)" 동일 한자, 한국어 역음 "두통". 어원: 頭 = 머리, 痛 = 아프다.

#### 예문

- **頭痛**がします。 — 두통이 있습니다. (증상, 캐주얼)
- **頭痛**がひどい場合は医者に診てもらってください。 — 두통이 심하면 의사에게 진료를 받으세요. (조언, 격식)
- **頭痛**薬 (ずつうぐすり) — 「두통약 (캐주얼)」

#### 관련 용어

- 頭痛 (ずつう) — 「두통 (일반)」
- 偏頭痛 (へんずつう) — 「편두통」
- 頭が痛い (あたまがいたい) — 「머리가 아프다 (캐주얼)」
- 頭痛薬 (ずつうぐすり) — 「두통약」
- [[health-vocabulary]] — 건강 어휘

#### 문화적 맥락

일본어 **頭痛 (ずつう)** 발음 "즈쓰-" — 한국어 "두통" (한자어) 와 발음 유사. 캐주얼: 頭痛 (zu-tsu-u) / 발음 변이: ずつう (촉음 っ). 한국어 "두통" / 한자어 "두통" 동일. **頭痛 (ずつう)** 발음의 촉음 っ (small つ) — 한국어 화자에게 연음 처리 연습. **頭 (あたま)** 발음은 頭 (head) 와 등 (back) 의 어원: 한자음 つ (頭) vs あたま (普通の). 발음: ずつう (zu-tsu-u) — 한국어 ㅈ + ㅅ + ㅜ 발음 연습.

#### 출처

- [[health-vocabulary]]

---

### 熱 (ねつ)

**품사:** 명사 (noun)

**정의:** 열 — 발열. 한국어 "열" (發熱) 의미 (한국어 "열"은 보통 fever).

**読み方 (읽는 법):** ねつ (히라가나) / netsu (로마자) / 熱 (한자, 音読み: ねつ netsu / ねっ netsu, 訓読み: あつ.い atsui)

**IPA / 발음:** /net͡sɯ/

**어원:** 漢字 "熱" (음읽 ねつ, 訓읽 あつ.い). 한국어 한자어 "열(熱)" 의미. 어원: 灬 (불/불볕) + 執 (집) → 불을 모음 → 열.

#### 예문

- 彼女は高い**熱**があります。 — 그녀는 높은 열이 있습니다. (증상, 격식)
- **熱**が下がりました。 — 열이 내렸습니다. (회복, 격식)
- **熱**があります。 — 열이 있습니다. (증상, 캐주얼)

#### 관련 용어

- 熱 (ねつ) — 「열 (발열)」
- 熱 (ねっ) — 「열 (촉음 변이, 단독)」
- 発熱 (はつねつ) — 「발열 (격식)」
- 熱がある (ねつがある) — 「열이 있다 (명사구)」
- [[health-vocabulary]] — 건강 어휘

#### 문화적 맥락

일본어 **熱 (ねつ)** 발음 "네쓰" — 한국어 "네쓰" (熱) 와 발음 동일. 캐주얼: 熱 (ne-tsu) / 격식: 発熱 (はつねつ). 한국어 "열" / 한자어 "열" 동일. **熱 (ねつ)** 와 **熱い (あつい, 뜨겁다)** 의 어원: 같은 한자 (熱) — 음읽 (ねつ) vs 훈읽 (あつい). 한국어 "열" (fever) / "뜨거움" (hot) 와 동일. **熱 (ねつ)** 가 발열, **熱 (あつい)** 가 더위. 발음: ねつ (ne-tsu) — 한국어 ㄴ + ㅅ + ㅅ 발음 연습.

#### 출처

- [[health-vocabulary]]

---

### 風邪 (かぜ)

**품사:** 명사 (noun)

**정의:** 감기 — 코·목 등의 감기. 한국어 "감기" 의미.

**読み方 (읽는 법):** かぜ (히라가나) / kaze (로마자) / 風邪 (한자, 音読み: ふうじゃ fuuja, 訓読み: かぜ kaze)

**IPA / 발음:** /ka.ze/

**어원:** 漢字 "風" (음읽 ふう/ふ, 訓읽 かぜ) + "邪" (음읽 じゃ, 訓읽 よこしま). 한국어 한자어 "풍사(風邪)" 의미. 어원: 風 = 바람, 邪 = 사기/기운.

#### 예문

- **風邪**を引きました。 — 감기에 걸렸습니다. (질병, 캐주얼)
- **風邪**が治りました。 — 감기가 나았습니다. (회복, 캐주얼)
- **風邪**をひいて学校を休みました。 — 감기에 걸려 학교를 쉬었습니다. (결석, 캐주얼)

#### 관련 용어

- 風邪 (かぜ) — 「감기 (캐주얼)」
- 風邪 (ふうじゃ) — 「감기 (격식)」
- 風邪薬 (かぜぐすり) — 「감기약」
- 風邪気味 (かぜぎみ) — 「감기 기미 (살짝)」
- [[health-vocabulary]] — 건강 어휘

#### 문화적 맥락

일본어 **風邪 (かぜ)** 발음 "카제" — 한국어 "카제" (風 + 邪) 와 발음 동일. 캐주얼: 風邪 (かぜ) / 격식: 風邪 (ふうじゃ). 한국어 "감기" (感冒) 의 어원: 중세 한국어 감기 (寒氣). **風邪 (かぜ)** 의 어원: 風 (바람) + 邪 (사기) = "바람의 사기" → 현대 의미 "감기". 한자어 어원 동일. 발음: かぜ (ka-ze) — 한국어 ㅋ + ㅈ 발음 연습. **風邪 (かぜ)** = 한국어 "감기" + **風邪 (かぜ, 바람)** 의 어원 차이.

#### 출처

- [[health-vocabulary]]

---

## 신체 (Body)

### 頭 (あたま)

**품사:** 명사 (noun)

**정의:** 머리 — 신체 머리 부분. 한국어 "머리" 의미.

**読み方 (읽는 법):** あたま (히라가나) / atama (로마자) / 頭 (한자, 音読み: とう tou / ず zu, 訓読み: あたま atama / かしら kashira)

**IPA / 발음:** /a.ta.ma/

**어원:** 漢字 "頭" (음읽 とう/ず, 訓읽 あたま/かしら). 한국어 한자어 "두(頭)" 의미. 어원: 豆 (콩) + 頁 (이마) → 이마 위의 작은 부분 → 머리.

#### 예문

- **頭**が痛みます。 — 머리가 아픕니다. (신체, 캐주얼)
- **頭**を使って考えましょう。 — 머리를 써서 생각해 봅시다. (사고, 격식)
- **頭**がいいです。 — 머리가 좋습니다 (똑똑함). (능력, 캐주얼)

#### 관련 용어

- 頭 (あたま) — 「머리 (캐주얼)」
- 頭 (かしら) — 「머리 (격식)」
- 頭 (ず) — 「머리 (음읽, 단독)」
- 頭部 (とうぶ) — 「두부 (의학)」
- 頭髪 (とうはつ) — 「두발 (머리카락)」
- [[health-vocabulary]] — 건강 어휘

#### 문화적 맥락

일본어 **頭 (あたま)** 발음 "아타마" — 한국어 "아타마" (순 우리말) 와 발음 동일. 캐주얼: あたま / 음읽: とう (頭) / ず (頭痛). 한국어 "머리" / 한자어 "두(頭)" 의미. **頭 (あたま)** + **頭 (かしら)** + **頭 (ず)** 의 어원: 모두 같은 한자 (頭) — 음읽 (とう/ず) vs 훈읽 (あたま/かしら). 한국어 "머리" / "두(頭)" 비교. 발음: あたま (a-ta-ma) — 한국어 ㄷ + ㅅ + ㅁ 발음 연습.

#### 출처

- [[health-vocabulary]]

---

### 胃 (い)

**품사:** 명사 (noun)

**정의:** 위 — 소화기. 한국어 "위" / 한자어 "위(胃)" 의미.

**読み方 (읽는 법):** い (히라가나) / i (로마자) / 胃 (한자, 音読み: い i)

**IPA / 발음:** /i/

**어원:** 漢字 "胃" (음읽 い). 한국어 한자어 "위(胃)" 의미. 어원: 月 (몸/달) + 田 (밭) → 몸속의 밭 (음식을 저장하는 장기) → 위.

#### 예문

- **胃**が痛みます。 — 위가 아픕니다. (통증, 캐주얼)
- **胃**カメラ (いカメラ) — 「위내시경 (캐주얼)」
- **胃**の検査を受けます。 — 위 검사를 받습니다. (검사, 격식)

#### 관련 용어

- 胃 (い) — 「위 (캐주얼)」
- 胃 (い) — 「위 (음읽, 단독)」
- 胃酸 (いさん) — 「위산」
- 胃炎 (いえん) — 「위염」
- 胃腸 (いちょう) — 「위장 (위+장)」
- [[health-vocabulary]] — 건강 어휘

#### 문화적 맥락

일본어 **胃 (い)** 발음 "이" — 한국어 "이" (이, 2) 와 발음 동일. 캐주얼: 胃 (i) / 음읽: 胃 (い). 한국어 "위" / 한자어 "위" (위) 동일. **胃 (い)** 발음 단일 모음 — 한국어 "위" (2음절) 와 다른 패턴. 한자 어원: 月 (몸) + 田 (밭) = "몸 안의 밭" (음식 저장) → 위. 발음: い (i) — 한국어 ㅣ 발음 연습.

#### 출처

- [[health-vocabulary]]

---

## 예약 (Appointment)

### 予約 (よやく)

**품사:** 명사 (noun) / する 동사

**정의:** 예약 — 미리 정함. 한국어 "예약" / 한자어 "예약(予約)" 의미.

**読み方 (읽는 법):** よやく (히라가나) / yoyaku (로마자) / 予約 (한자, 音読み: よやく yoyaku)

**IPA / 발음:** /jo.ja.kɯ/

**어원:** 漢字 "予" (음읽 よ/しゃ, 訓읽 あらかじ.め) + "約" (음읽 やく, 訓읽 つづ.まる/つづ.める). 한국어 한자어 "예약(予約)" 동일 한자, 한국어 역음 "예약". 어원: 予 = 미리, 約 = 정함.

#### 예문

- 医者の**予約**があります。 — 의사 예약이 있습니다. (예약, 격식)
- **予約**をお願いします。 — 예약 부탁합니다. (요청, 캐주얼)
- **予約**をキャンセルします。 — 예약을 취소합니다. (취소, 캐주얼)

#### 관련 용어

- 予約 (よやく) — 「예약 (명사)」
- 予約する (よやくする) — 「예약하다 (동사)」
- 予約済み (よやくずみ) — 「예약 완료」
- 予約金 (よやくきん) — 「예약금」
- [[health-vocabulary]] — 건강 어휘

#### 문화적 맥락

일본어 **予約 (よやく)** 발음 "요야쿠" — 한국어 "예약" (한자어) 와 발음 동일. 캐주얼: 予約 (yo-ya-ku) / 동사: 予約する (よやくする). 한국어 "예약" / 한자어 "예약" 동일. 일본 의료 **予約 (예약)** = 한국어 "예약" 동일. **予約 (예약)** 시스템: **ネット予約 (넷 예약)** = 한국어 "온라인 예약" 빈번. 발음: よやく (yo-ya-ku) — 한국어 ㅇ + ㅇ + ㄱ 발음 연습.

#### 출처

- [[health-vocabulary]]

---

## 파이프라인 형태 (기계 판독 가능)

> 하류 소비자용으로 생성됨 (`Game/typing_language/raw/jp_words.md`).
